A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching authors, core scoring methods and original experiments. The text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are available and readable, supporting a reliable comparison despite substantial additions in v4.

before.justification: v2 reports original MMLU head-zeroing experiments across 14 models, score-function overlap measurements, attention-score distributions and attention-pattern analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds PIQA and WinoGrande evaluations, projected-output scoring comparisons, layer-wise analyses and growing-context experiments.

M1.justification: The original scoring and dynamic head-zeroing procedures remain. Appendix A.1 adds implemented circuit-based AHON variants that score head contributions after output projection, changing the quantities used to select heads. Head normalization is retained in Appendix A.2 and intervention plots; its disappearance from the main text does not constitute method removal.

E1.justification: v2 evaluates intervention accuracy on MMLU and uses FineWeb-Edu for attention analyses. v4 adds PIQA physical commonsense reasoning and WinoGrande pronoun resolution across all 14 models, substantially broadening the evaluated task requirements beyond the original knowledge benchmark.

E2.justification: v4 Figure 7 adds circuit-based AHON and its layer-normalized variant to the MMLU comparison. Figures 2–3 exclude Last Token Head Output Norm (HN) from the overlap and ranking comparisons, although it remains in appendix intervention grids. AWFT and random-zeroing baselines are retained.

E3.justification: The existing 14-model, 5-shot MMLU and seven-threshold protocol remains. New designs include 0-shot PIQA, 5-shot WinoGrande, dataset-specific threshold calibration to identify 15% of heads for layer comparisons, and tracking growing prefixes of three FineWeb-Edu sequences of at least 512 tokens. These substantially extend the controlled evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained overlap, distribution, scaling, finetuning and PCA analyses, v4 adds an output-projection ablation (A.1), cross-dataset layer profiles (4.4), examples identified by individual scoring rules (A.3), and context-dependent inactivity curves and masks (A.5). These investigate sensitivity to output definition, dataset and increasing context.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for the intervention evaluations. The added experiments continue reporting point results and curves without uncertainty estimates; the score-distribution histograms are behavioral analyses.

E6.justification: MMLU Table 2 is unchanged, including average removable-head fractions of 4.61% for AWFT and 12.18% for Ours. v4 adds PIQA results of 10.01% versus 21.38% and WinoGrande results of 6.90% versus 14.45%, plus circuit-based, layer-wise and context-dependent findings. These are substantial additional results under distinct conditions.

T1.justification: v4 Appendix A.1 adds a formal definition of projected head contributions and derives the block decomposition of the output projection in Equations 2–3. It also explains why zeroing a fixed head removes its contribution under either output definition. The original scoring equations remain, and the added mathematical treatment is limited in scope.

C1.justification: The abstract and first contribution shift from proposing a taxonomy of 13 functions to evaluating 12 principal score functions, modestly narrowing the headline contribution. The central claims about over 12% inactivity, AWFT underestimation, output-norm scoring and limited finetuning effects remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations of dataset stability, AWFT's decline with growing context and the role of output projection. Appendix A.14 substantially clarifies applicability: AHON requires computing head outputs, so zeroing them does not itself save that computation, and multiple-choice interventions do not establish reliable generation. It also discusses routing and cache-compression possibilities.

D1.justification: v4 adds a stated code-repository location, exact FineWeb-Edu sequence identifiers, projected-output implementation details and descriptions of the added datasets. Existing PyTorch intervention steps, model dtypes and automatic batch-size guidance are retained. These are useful but localized reproducibility additions.

R1.justification: v4 adds references for PIQA, WinoGrande, transformer circuits, runtime neural pruning and mixture-of-depths. These extend discussion toward circuit interpretations and conditional computation. The main positioning relative to attention sinks, dormant heads and earlier head-pruning research remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. v4 standardizes score-function terminology, reframes Section 3, expands the normalization explanation and moves head normalization and short scoring-rule descriptions into the appendix. The new analyses receive dedicated subsections, while editing of retained material remains localized.

P2.justification: v4 adds layer profiles, circuit comparisons, example-head panels, two complete benchmark grids, context-length curves and inactivity masks, together with three result tables. It also simplifies Table 1, revises the main comparison matrices and replaces repeated legends in the full MMLU grid with a shared legend. These substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially addresses v2's reliance on MMLU for intervention validation by adding two distinct tasks across all 14 models. The projection ablation and dataset/context analyses strengthen the evidence, while explicit computational and generation limitations improve the interpretation of retained claims. The gains concern validation and clarity rather than improved MMLU scores. Generalization remains bounded: AWFT still wins several rows in Tables 4–5, and generation is unevaluated.
